mechanism_narrative: The sustained high residential mobility, consistently above baseline, indicates a prevailing preference for staying home, which will continue to suppress out-of-home activities and thus keep retail and recreation mobility lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in transit station usage, indicating a return to commuting and general movement, will directly translate to increased footfall in retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT mobility rises by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, even if TRANSIT mobility rises by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined recovery in both workplace attendance and visits to parks signifies a broader societal shift towards increased outdoor and public engagement, which will positively impact retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and PARKS both show week-on-week increases for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite both WORKPLACES and PARKS showing consecutive week-on-week increases.

mechanism_narrative: In the absence of new or tightening mobility restrictions, the current suppressed state of retail and recreation mobility is likely at a floor, suggesting a gradual rebound as consumer confidence slowly returns over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, even if no new restrictions are announced or implemented.

mechanism_narrative: The stagnation of retail and recreation mobility at a significantly low level for the past two weeks indicates a strong inertia in consumer behavior, which will prevent any significant recovery in the immediate two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is significantly higher (e.g., >5 percentage points) than over the last 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp and immediate decline in residential mobility, indicating a sudden shift away from staying at home, will quickly translate into increased out-of-home activities and a rapid rise in retail and recreation mobility within the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than over the last 7 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility falling by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent combination of elevated grocery and pharmacy visits (essential trips) and high residential mobility suggests a continued cautious behavior focused on necessities and staying home, which will suppress discretionary retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than over the last 14 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated.

mechanism_narrative: In a context of gradual reopening, the recent slight increases in transit and workplace mobility suggest an immediate, albeit small, return to daily routines that will provide a short-term boost to retail and recreation mobility within the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increased week-on-week in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than over the last 7 days, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing week-on-week increases in t-0w.
